attribution_limitations: Caption dates for Figure 1 panels A (July 11) and B (August 7), 2021 do not match the narrative, which places the Panel A CT in the June 2021 index admission and the Panel B CT at the July 2021 readmission 21 days after discharge. Dates are kept as stated in the caption and are not reconciled with the narrative months or each other; panel C (September 11) and D (December 8) fall within the August-December 2021 follow-up.

Final radiological outcome is called complete resolution in the abstract and body but near-complete with minimal residual changes in the Figure 1 caption. Both are retained; complete is the accepted outcome fact and the caption wording is held as a review-only conflict.
Follow-up duration is "five months" in the abstract but given as serial CT between August and December 2021 in the body; exact scan dates other than the caption dates are not stated.

Readmission CRP is called "mildly increased" (2.75 mg/dL; Table 1 prints 2,75 against reference <0.5) while the stay is summarized as having consistently low inflammatory markers; both statements are kept as written and not reconciled. Table 1 uses decimal commas in 2,75 and 28,2.

The post-COVID cavitation attribution is the authors' clinical judgement; no biopsy or pathology supports viral necrosis or microangiopathy, and Discussion mechanisms (secondary infection, microthrombosis, other published cases) are background, not facts about this patient. Whether the empiric intravenous antibiotics started at readmission are the "antimicrobial therapy" later discontinued is implied, not stated. Table 1 "-" cells (index-admission BAL and immunology) are not documented results and were not converted to facts. The article states this case was previously shown as a congress poster (13th Iberian Pneumology Congress, 2022); that is a same-case disclosure, not a second patient.

The readmission empiric intravenous antibiotics are reported in the same sentence as the initially considered probable lung abscess, joined only by "and"; no indication is explicitly stated, so none is recorded on the medication. Likewise the index-admission corticosteroids and broad-spectrum antibiotics carry no recorded indication (abstract ties the triad to severe COVID-19 pneumonia; body to hypercapnic respiratory failure).

He developed acute hypercapnic respiratory failure requiring noninvasive ventilation, and received systemic corticosteroids and empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics. He improved and was discharged. Table 1 records his index-admission blood counts, inflammatory/coagulation markers, renal/liver tests and room-air arterial blood gas.
